title: App Studio vs Dev Studio
learning_objectives: Understand the differences between App Studio and Dev Studio
Learn when to use each development environment
Understand the target users for each tool

introduction.title: Two Development Environments
introduction.text: PEGA provides two primary development environments: App Studio and Dev Studio. Each is designed for different types of users and development scenarios. Understanding when and how to use each tool is crucial for effective PEGA development. This tutorial will help you understand the differences and choose the right tool for your needs.

sections.title: App Studio Overview
sections.content: App Studio is PEGA's low-code development environment designed primarily for business users, citizen developers, and those new to PEGA development.
target_users: Business analysts and subject matter experts
Citizen developers with limited technical background
New PEGA developers learning the platform
Business users who need to make quick changes

main_capabilities.description: Create and configure case types using visual designers and guided workflows.
Design business processes using drag-and-drop flow designers with pre-built templates.
Create user interfaces using visual form designers and pre-built components.
Define data structures using simplified property editors and data relationship tools.
Create business rules using guided decision trees and condition builders.

sections.title: Dev Studio Overview
sections.content: Dev Studio is PEGA's comprehensive development environment designed for professional developers, system architects, and advanced users who need full access to PEGA's capabilities.
key_characteristics: Complete access to all PEGA rules and features
target_users: Advanced business users with technical skills

main_capabilities.description: Create and modify any type of PEGA rule with full configuration options.
Configure complex integrations with external systems and services.
Access performance monitoring tools and optimization features.
Configure advanced security settings, access controls, and authentication.
Manage system settings, deployment, and maintenance tasks.

sections.title: Detailed Comparison
sections.content: Here's a detailed comparison of App Studio and Dev Studio across various dimensions.

comparison_table.app_studio: Modern, simplified interface with guided workflows and wizards
comparison_table.dev_studio: Comprehensive interface with access to all features and detailed configuration options

comparison_table.app_studio: Gentle learning curve, designed for non-technical users
comparison_table.dev_studio: Steeper learning curve, requires technical knowledge and PEGA experience

comparison_table.app_studio: Faster for standard use cases with pre-built templates and guided processes
comparison_table.dev_studio: Slower initial development but more flexibility for complex requirements

comparison_table.app_studio: Limited customization options, focuses on best practices and standards
comparison_table.dev_studio: Unlimited customization with access to all PEGA capabilities

comparison_table.app_studio: Access to commonly used rules with simplified editors
comparison_table.dev_studio: Access to all rule types with full configuration options
Advanced debugging tools, performance monitoring, and diagnostic features

comparison_table.app_studio: Designed for business-IT collaboration with shared terminology
comparison_table.dev_studio: Technical collaboration with detailed change tracking and version control

sections.title: When to Use App Studio
sections.content: App Studio is the right choice for specific scenarios and user types.

use_cases.description: If you're new to PEGA, App Studio provides a gentler introduction with guided workflows and built-in best practices.
benefits: Guided workflows ensure proper development practices

use_cases.description: For typical business applications that follow standard patterns, App Studio provides faster development.
benefits: Pre-built templates for common use cases

use_cases.description: When business users need to be actively involved in development or make changes themselves.
For quickly creating prototypes or proof-of-concept applications.

sections.title: When to Use Dev Studio
sections.content: Dev Studio is necessary for advanced scenarios and complex requirements.

use_cases.description: When you need to integrate with multiple external systems or implement complex integration patterns.
When standard App Studio capabilities aren't sufficient for your requirements.
For system configuration, maintenance, and administrative tasks.
For large-scale enterprise applications with complex requirements.

sections.title: Navigating App Studio
sections.content: Understanding App Studio's interface and navigation will help you work more effectively.

interface_elements.description: The main navigation panel showing your application structure, case types, and development artifacts.
key_features: Quick access to case types and processes

interface_elements.description: The main work area where you design processes, forms, and configure application components.
Context-sensitive panels that show properties and configuration options for selected elements.
Action buttons and tools for common development tasks.

sections.title: Navigating Dev Studio
sections.content: Dev Studio has a more complex interface that provides access to all PEGA capabilities.

interface_elements.description: Comprehensive navigation with access to all PEGA tools and administrative functions.
Detailed view of all rules in your application with search and filtering capabilities.
Tabbed interface for editing multiple rules simultaneously.

sections.title: Best Practices for Tool Selection
sections.content: Follow these best practices to choose the right tool for your development needs.

practices.description: Begin new projects in App Studio to leverage guided workflows and best practices.
practices.rationale: App Studio enforces good development practices and provides a structured approach to application development.

practices.practice: Switch to Dev Studio When Needed
practices.description: Move to Dev Studio when you encounter limitations or need advanced features.
Leverage both tools in the same project based on the task at hand.
practices.approach: Business users can work in App Studio while developers use Dev Studio for advanced features.

practices.description: Choose tools based on your team's technical expertise and comfort level.

summary.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Studio is designed for business users and low-code development
Dev Studio provides complete access to all PEGA capabilities
Choose tools based on user expertise and project requirements
Both tools can be used collaboratively in the same project
Start with App Studio and move to Dev Studio as needed
Understanding both tools makes you a more effective PEGA developer

next_steps.title: What's Next?
next_steps.text: Now that you understand the differences between App Studio and Dev Studio, the next tutorial will guide you through creating your first case application using App Studio's guided approach.
